images.filename: Merrimack Canal, Lowell MA, Aug. 1921 (62b80d7b-2dbf-4b67-9a29-f1147f797eb5).jpg
images.caption:
A photo showing the Merrimack Canal
One of the most iconic scenes in Lowell, the photo shows the Moody Street feeder Gatehouse at far left, the Dutton Street boardinghouses along the left of the canal, and Lowell High School to the right. The canal was completed in 1823 to power the Merrimack Manufacturing Company.
Keywords: Lowell

images.filename: A Rail Car Slipped Off the Rails, Nov. 9, 1917 (a43a7dab-3036-46b1-b5e2-40c5ab92c28c).jpg
images.caption:
A photo showing a disabled rail car.
The car was loaded with 100 bales of cotton for the Boott Mills. This challenging section of curved track was one of many tight turns in the densely packed city. Originally sited to take advantage of waterpower before railroads came into use, each mill was eventually served by railroads to carry in raw materials and coal. This section of track and its "S" curve is still in use. Lowell NHP trolleys travel this section of track (and manage to stay on the track) on daily runs between the Visitor Center and the Boott Cotton Mills Museum.
Keywords: Lowell

images.filename: Looking up John St. from the entrance to the Boott Mills, Aug. 9, 1924 (fd0bf1c1-1b0c-4767-b4f1-86308b157cbd).JPG
images.caption:
A photo showing workers repairing a bridge.
Workers repair the bridge over the Eastern Canal. If you visit the Boott Cotton Mills Museum at Lowell National Historical Park, you can stand at this same viewpoint, but the view is a bit different today. The boardinghouses on either side of John St. are gone; to the right of John St. is Boardinghouse Park, to the left, a parking lot for the residents of Boott Mills condominiums.
Keywords: Lowell; engineering; Merrimack River; Boott Mills
